state_doh_release.mode:
Mississippi State Department of Health Authorizes Expanded Syringe Services Program Coverage
The Department has approved expansion of authorized syringe services programs to additional counties under Mississippi public health authority. Syringe services programs reduce transmission of HIV and hepatitis C, connect individuals to medication for opioid use disorder, and distribute naloxone and fentanyl test strips. Decades of peer-reviewed evidence and CDC guidance support syringe services programs as a core component of the public health response to drug-related harms.

steps.name: Validate Loaded Data
steps.goal: Confirm the loaded DataFrame matches the profiled schema (shape, dtypes, column names).
success_criteria: DataFrame shape matches data_profile.n_rows and n_columns
risks: File re-read may differ from the profiled version

steps.name: Exploratory Data Analysis
steps.goal: Produce distribution summaries, correlation/association analysis, and a missing-value overview.
success_criteria: Distribution summary produced for numeric features
risks: High-cardinality columns may produce unusable plots

steps.name: Pre-Modeling Leakage Audit
steps.goal: Audit feature candidates and column names for leakage before any split or transformation.
success_criteria: All potential ID columns confirmed excluded from feature_candidates
risks: An ID or encoded-target column may have been retained in features

steps.name: Split Data and Fit Transformers
steps.goal: Split into train/val/test with seed=42; fit imputer/encoder on X_train only.
success_criteria: Split performed before any transformer is fitted
Transformer fit called only on X_train
risks: fit_transform on full data → leakage
Unset seed → non-reproducible splits

steps.name: Train Baseline DummyRegressor (mean)
steps.goal: Establish a performance floor with DummyRegressor (mean); record rmse, mae, r2 on validation.
success_criteria: Baseline metrics (rmse, mae, r2) recorded with split 'val'
risks: Evaluating baseline on the test set instead of val

steps.name: Train Candidate Model
steps.goal: Train task-conditioned candidate models and select the best on validation.
success_criteria: Model selected on validation only (test untouched)
candidate val RMSE < baseline val RMSE
risks: Tuning may leak test data if not isolated

steps.name: Final Evaluation
steps.goal: Evaluate the selected model on held-out data; produce the required artifacts and a baseline comparison.
risks: Reporting val metrics as final

steps.name: Interpret Drivers
steps.goal: Compute feature importance / key patterns; list caveats. No causal language.
risks: Importance reflects associations, not causation

steps.name: Generate Final Report
steps.goal: Write the structured report referencing real artifact paths and metric values.
success_criteria: Every metric includes its split label
risks: Metric values copied incorrectly from state

steps.name: Independent Report Review
steps.goal: Audit the report against state; verify claims, metrics, and artifact references.
success_criteria: Every metric in report matches state.evaluation
risks: Subtle causal framing may pass without careful reading

evaluation.selection_rationale: Selected by block_mae on the internal holdout.

key_findings: 3 columns have missing values; highest is state_doh_release (29.6%).

caveats: Importance is associative (|correlation| for numeric features), not causal.

residual_analysis.heteroscedasticity_note: strong positive — errors grow with predicted values

schema_comparison.note: 0 column(s) only in training data (may include target components); 1 column(s) only in prediction data.

target_distribution.interpretation: heavily right-skewed — log-transform of target may help

cross_feature_target_patterns.note: Top interaction effects between time features and low-cardinality features. interaction_strength = max_level_time_range - min_level_time_range; level_spread = max_level_mean - min_level_mean.

recommendations: Target is right-skewed (skewness=2.70): consider log-transform; MAE on raw target will weight large values heavily.
